analysis.title: US Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (Nov 24, 2026)
key_insights: NVDA reinstated Jensen Huang after apparent political pressure, triggering a sharp AI trade reversal. SMH rose about 15%, essentially erasing Friday's losses, with the most funding-sensitive names such as CRWV and ORCL gaining most.

Desk sees a new AI Put / Trump Put. It lowers uncertainty around AI ecosystem financing but not around chip export restrictions or revenue impact. Corporate governance and political-involvement uncertainty rose sharply.
Pre-market Nov 24 futures are lower. SPX -0.7%, NDX -1.5%, RTY -0.3%, with Semis and Memory down 4-6%. The market is testing whether Monday was a deadcat bounce or the start of a sustainable rally.

Flash PMIs missed expectations but remain strong, pointing to about 3% real GDP growth in 26Q4 versus 3.4% in 26Q3. Inflation and supply disruptions persist. The desk says markets should return to pricing three consecutive 25bp hikes from Dec 2026 to Mar 2027.

Flows were as expected after the NVDA news. Aggressive covering in memory and hardware, long-only buyers adding back to NVDA, crowded shorts leading, and Info Tech the leading buyer sector on +20% volume.

Staples flow skews better-to-buy with long-only demand in WMT, PFGC, MNST and TJX. Staples L/S positioning is about the 80th percentile over 12 months but about the 30th percentile since 2018, so not historically crowded. XLP is +16% YTD.

A buyside poll found most respondents see the rally as a deadcat or bear-market bounce capable of a squeeze. Consumer discretionary was the most popular buy, then semis. The squeeze could extend if short cover turns into long chase and then CTA buying.

D1 Thematic: 2027 favors selective risk over indiscriminate risk-on. Trade idea is long the Interest Coverage Pair JPUPINTC (long high coverage, short low coverage). Credit already shows the divide via widened CCC/BB dispersion, and equities have not yet followed.

US Market Intel moves back to Tactically Cautious. It admits missing the tactical bullish call, sees a tactical bounce as likely but not a bottom, and cites 2018 as the best comp, where the late-year bounce was faded.
Fundamentals remain supportive. SPX median 26Q3 earnings growth was about 12% versus a 10-year average of 12.6% (FactSet), and median profit margins hit fresh ATHs.

Monetization Menu (Nov 23) is market-neutral. Mag7 and security software are the safest Tech areas, use options for a memory/semis rebound, and longer term own +SPW vs -SPX or -NDX. UK/EU should outperform on dollar profit-taking, and Value beats Beta and Momentum.

Dubravko reiterates a YE26 SPX target of 8,000 ($365 EPS, 21.9x), published Nov 6. Ideas are long 12M momentum vs short 3M momentum, AI upstream attractive after the positioning flush, low vol less compelling, and consumer cyclicals challenged by affordability.

Calendar: US Market Intel is off Nov 25-27 and returns Nov 30. Key events are DELL earnings Nov 24, PCE and GDP Nov 25, NFP Dec 4, FOMC Dec 9, CPI Dec 10, government funding deadline Dec 11, and G20 Dec 15-16.

risk_factors: Decline in the incremental buyer and a positioning purge.
Hawkish Fed narrative and nascent hiking cycles hurting FY27 and FY28 earnings.
Uncertainty over chip export restrictions and sales impact.
SEC accounting probe and political involvement in corporate governance may weigh on equity multiples.
Another surge in USD could temper European outperformance.
vol_and_positioning: Staples L/S positioning about 80th percentile vs last 12 months and about 30th percentile since 2018.
Consensus shorts rallied more than 1 sigma over the past month, driving the low-quality rebound.
Crowded shorts (JPSQZZ) led the NVDA-day move, with aggressive covering in memory and hardware.
Tech trades are getting increasingly crowded, creating pain risk if a tactical Tech bounce comes.
Neither institutional nor retail flows supported a material rise in bullishness Monday. Systematic buying could turn the deadcat into a tactical rally.
Options recommended to play a memory/semis rebound given squeeze risk.
Low Vol factor moved from 0th to 25th percentile, making it less compelling.
geopolitical: US administration reportedly pressured NVDA to reinstate Jensen Huang, with Bessent tone shift and a Trump Truth Social post.
The administration is said to be considering tighter chip sales restrictions to China.
US and China agreed to extend the trade truce through January 20, 2027.
California probe into Nvidia covers potential criminal law violations, and a Democratic-majority Congress is expected to prioritize investigations.
G20 Summit in Miami Dec 15-16 and US government funding deadline Dec 11.

tension_points.bull_case: Government backing of AI creates a new market put, positioning is washed out, and short cover to long chase to CTA buying could extend the squeeze.
tension_points.bear_case: Most buyside respondents see a deadcat bounce, Tech fundamentals and 2028 visibility are uncertain, and 2018 is the comp where the late-year bounce was faded.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bullish flip requires positioning reset, Cyclicals outperforming Defensives, lower vol, or a Fed pause in December.
